newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end mixed, S&Ps ease late.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end mixed, S&Ps ease late.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished mixed, with Standard & Poor's 500s closing slightly lower after the rally that drove March to all-time highs petered out in thin holiday trade.

"Making new contract highs and then closing nearly unchanged does not bode well for stocks," one S&P futures floor source said. "If bonds don't giddy-up on Tuesday, this market is heading lower for the rest of the week."
The Martin Luther King Jr holiday in the U.S. shut the U.S. bond and currency futures markets, and contributed to illiquid trading conditions in the S&P 500 market, traders said.
March S&Ps lost momentum after retesting the contract and all-time high of 784.60 in late afternoon trade. Some traders were expecting March to test resistance at 785.50 and 786.75.
One trader said the 786.75 level represents a trendline level from mid-1996.
Small institutional buying lifted both March S&Ps and March Nasdaq 100s, and touched off a wave of local short-covering in the pits, they said.
"Locals continue to try to pick tops," one floor source said about local traders' inclination towards accumulating short positions.
Not only did locals scramble to cover those shorts, but buy-stop orders were touched off as March S&Ps rallied through 782.40. The 782.40 level was the previous contract high set on GLOBEX.
One U.S. firm also turned into a strong buyer after selling contracts at the opening.
Traders said the strength in the U.S. dollar, coupled with expectations for good quarterly earnings from high-tech companies and major banks, gave the market a firm underlying tone.
The U.S. stock market is also riding on strong seasonal factors, said James Stack, president of InvestTech Research.
"We have one, possibly two more weeks, of seasonal strength ahead of us, and how well we stand after that remains to be seen," Stack said.
He said concerns about a possible rate hike or a bias towards a tightening at the February 4-5 Federal Open Market Committee meeting could surface and weigh on stocks.
"The stock market has discounted no action (in monetary policy)," he said. "But I have to believe the Federal Reserve is getting more nervous as the Dow approaches 7,000."
Meanwhile, Nikkei 225 futures continued to grind lower throughout the day. March Nikkeis fell to a session low of 17,310, and closer to the contract low of 17,265.
Fair value for March S&Ps stood at 4.60 points over the cash index, with arbitrage buy programs at a 5.80-point premium and arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 3.20 points to cash, traders said.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps closed down 0.60 at 780.15, KCBT Value Lines were off 0.30 at 707.20, NYSE Composites were off 0.60 at 411.05, Nikkeis were off 780 at 17,340 and Nasdaq 100s were up 17.10 at 907.60.
